newsitem.title: USA: Elf Atochem raising Kynar PVDF capacity.
newsitem.headline: Elf Atochem raising Kynar PVDF capacity.

text.p: Elf Atochem, which markets polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) under the trade name Kynar, said Thursday it is increasing manufacturing capacities 25 percent over the four years.

The Elf Aquitaine subsidiary said new capacities are due to come on stream in the second half of 1996 at Pierre Benite in France and in early 1998 at Calvert City, Ky. Further expansion is being studied for the year 2000 in order to meet projected market growth.
Elf Atochem said it is also increasing capacities for vinylidene fluoride (VF2), a raw material for Kynar resin.
Capital expenditures for these projects are estimated to be 90 million FF ($18 million), the company said.

Kynar resin is used as a piping and lining material in the chemical processing industry because of its excellent chemical resistance and high purity; in the electrical industry as a jacket material for plenum-rated fiber optic, data and telephone cables; and in the coatings industry as the base resin for premium architectural coatings that provide superior fade and chalk resistance.
